title: Under :httpc one slow query stalls every other request
description: The httpc adapter sets max_keep_alive_length: 100, so httpc queues concurrent requests onto one keep-alive session instead of opening another. A request that TypeDB holds — waiting on the schema lock, a long analytical read — therefore blocks every other request on that connection behind it. Measured against 3.12.1 with a :schema transaction held open for 500ms: under Finch the blocked one-shot takes 503ms and a concurrent :read takes 2ms; under :httpc both sit until the 10s request timeout and the blocked one fails outright. max_keep_alive_length: 0 fixes it (blocked 557ms, unblocked 5ms); 1 is not enough (508ms). This contradicts 'requests run in the calling process, so N processes issue N concurrent requests' for anyone on the OTP-only transport.
acceptance_criteria: A concurrent request is not delayed by a slow one under any adapter, the default is changed rather than documented as a workaround, throughput is re-measured to show what the change costs, and a test covers it.
close_reason: :max_keep_alive_length now defaults to 0, so :httpc never queues a request behind one already in flight. Verified against a live server (blocked 557ms / unblocked 5ms, against 10s timeouts for both before) and by a unit test that runs a slow request beside a fast one through all three adapters, confirmed to fail on the old default. Concurrent throughput improved as well: 437 req/s vs 368 at 64-way.

title: Settle Duration.to_iso8601/1 on a negative component
description:
The single call the audit left open. to_iso8601/1 raises a %TypeDB.Error{} for
a negative months/days/nanos rather than emitting "P-1Y-2M", which its own
parse/1 rejects and which TypeDB misparses as a type label. The alternatives
are returning {:error, reason} - a signature change, so it must happen before
1.0 or never - or normalising silently.

Only reachable from a hand-built struct; TypeDB never sends a negative
duration. Low stakes, but the signature is frozen at 1.0, so the decision is
not deferrable.
design:
Decision: to_iso8601/1 keeps raising, and the error kind is corrected from :config to a new :encode.

Rejected returning {:ok, string} | {:error, _}: Elixir's own renderers raise (Date.to_iso8601/1 does), and no duration the driver produces can be negative — parse/1 never yields one and TypeDB never sends one — so every caller would be made to handle a case only a hand-built struct can reach.

Rejected normalising silently: it would send a value nobody asked for.

What was actually wrong was the kind. :config is documented as 'the driver was configured incorrectly, raised at start-up', and this is neither. :encode is the mirror of the existing :decode: :decode is a response body that could not become Elixir terms, :encode is an Elixir term that cannot become a TypeDB wire value. The three raises in TypeDB.Given were mislabelled the same way and move with it.

The kind is now asserted in the tests rather than assumed, because 1.0 freezes Error.kind().
close_reason: Keeps raising; kind corrected to the new :encode, which also fixes the three mislabelled raises in TypeDB.Given. Decision recorded in the issue.

title: Hide internal modules from the published docs
description:
TypeDB.Wire, TypeDB.Bang, TypeDB.Transport and TypeDB.Token are implementation
detail. Rendered on hexdocs they read as public surface, and after 1.0 someone
will depend on them. @moduledoc false, or an explicit "internal, no stability
guarantee" note for the ones worth reading.
close_reason: Transport and Token are @moduledoc false; groups_for_modules updated; mix docs is warning-free.

title: Add an API snapshot test
description:
SemVer is currently a promise kept by attention. Render every public module,
function, arity and spec into a checked-in snapshot file and fail the build when
the two disagree. Changing the API then requires changing the snapshot in the
same commit, which is exactly the moment to ask whether it is a minor or a
major.

The machinery already exists: test/typedb/api_convention_test.exs uses
Code.Typespec.fetch_specs/1 and spec_to_quoted/2 to walk the surface.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot committed; a deliberate signature change fails the suite with a readable diff; CONTRIBUTING explains how to update it and how to classify the change.
close_reason: Snapshot test plus test/api_snapshot.txt; regeneration documented in CONTRIBUTING; guard verified by mutating a spec.

title: Add operation-level telemetry spans
description:
lib/typedb/telemetry.ex:10 is explicit: one span per HTTP request, including
each retry and each renew-and-retry. So [:typedb, :request, :stop] counts
attempts, not queries. A dashboard built on it cannot answer how long a query
took end to end, how many queries the application ran, or what fraction needed
a retry - the three questions anyone actually asks.

Add [:typedb, :query, :start|:stop|:exception] and [:typedb, :transaction, ...]
around the whole logical operation, with the per-attempt spans nested inside
and unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: New spans documented in TypeDB.Telemetry with their metadata; existing :request spans unchanged; a test asserts one operation span per query regardless of the number of attempts.
close_reason: Operation and transaction spans added, documented, and tested; :route added to keep metric tags bounded.

title: Cap the backoff delay with :retry_max_delay
description:
Exponential growth is unbounded. With the documented default base and
max_retries: 10, the last sleep is over 50 seconds - inside the caller process,
holding whatever that process holds. Nothing in the config can currently stop
it.

Add :retry_max_delay (default in the low single-digit seconds), applied after
jitter, validated by Config.parse_timeout/3 like every other timeout.
close_reason: :retry_max_delay added, default 5s, caps every backoff form including a caller function; exponential now integer-shift and clamped.

title: Bound the total time of a request, not just each attempt
description:
Today :timeout means one attempt. The worst case a caller actually
experiences is timeout * (max_retries + 1) + the sum of the backoffs. A caller
that writes timeout: 5_000 and reads the docs still gets a call that can block
for well over half a minute, and there is no option that says otherwise.

This is the item that must land before 1.0 whatever the answer, because both
candidate answers change the meaning of an existing documented option:
  (a) add :deadline as a wall-clock budget, each attempt getting min(:timeout,
      remaining) - additive, two knobs to explain;
  (b) redefine :timeout as the budget for the whole operation and derive the
      per-attempt timeout - one knob, but a silent behaviour change for anyone
      already relying on the current meaning.

Decide, write down why, then implement.
design:
Chose (a): a new :deadline option, default :infinity, rather than redefining :timeout.

:timeout is documented as the per-attempt receive timeout and is handed straight to the HTTP adapter as exactly that. Redefining it as a whole-operation budget would silently change behaviour for everyone already relying on the documented meaning, and would make the per-attempt timeout implicit — derived, unexplainable, and different for every attempt.

Two knobs with one job each is the smaller cost. :timeout bounds an attempt, :deadline bounds the call. Each attempt is given min(timeout, remaining), a retry that cannot finish inside the budget is not started, and the deadline error carries the failure that prompted the give-up so 'deadline reached' never hides whether the server was down or merely slow.

Default :infinity keeps 0.1.0 behaviour intact; with :retry_max_delay now capping the backoff, the default worst case is finite and stateable without it.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded in the issue; option implemented and validated; a test proves a request cannot exceed the budget across retries; TypeDB moduledoc states the worst case arithmetic explicitly.
close_reason: Added :deadline (connection-level and per-call on every function that takes :timeout). Decision recorded in the issue design notes.

title: Add jitter to the default backoff
description:
lib/typedb/config.ex:238 returns trunc(base * 2^(attempt-1)) exactly. Every
caller that fails at the same instant - which is what a server restart, a
network blip or a rolling deploy produces - waits exactly the same number of
milliseconds and retries in lockstep, repeatedly, for as many attempts as
:max_retries allows. That is the textbook thundering herd, and it makes the
driver an amplifier of the outage it is trying to ride out.

Full jitter (sleep a uniform random value in [0, delay]) is the default in the
AWS SDKs, Finch, Tesla and Oban for the same reason. Determinism stays
available through the existing :retry_backoff function form, which tests
already use.
acceptance_criteria: Default backoff is jittered; a test asserts the spread over many attempts rather than a fixed value; the function form of :retry_backoff is still honoured verbatim; TypeDB moduledoc documents the default.
close_reason: Full jitter on {:exponential, _}; function form unchanged. Tests assert the ceiling and the absence of lockstep.

title: Observability: telemetry spans and logging that survive production
description:
Telemetry today is one span per HTTP attempt and five Logger call sites across
four modules. You can measure attempts; you cannot measure operations, you
cannot see a give-up, and you cannot turn any of it down without touching the
host application Logger config.
close_reason: Operation and transaction spans, richer metadata, :log_level, warnings on give-up and failed renewal, the retry-exhausted event, and attach_default_logger/1.

title: Freeze the public API for 1.0
description:
1.0.0 is a promise about the surface, so the surface has to be deliberate and
mechanically defended. Includes the one judgement call the audit left open.
close_reason: API snapshot test, internals hidden, Duration and analyze decisions settled, ConceptRow.to_struct/2 added, versioning policy written.

title: Retry, timeout and backoff semantics fit for production
description:
1.0.0 freezes defaults, and every item here IS a default. Changing any of them
afterwards is a major bump, so they have to be right before the tag.

The driver retries inside the caller process (lib/typedb/transport.ex:126-158)
with a pure exponential backoff (lib/typedb/config.ex:238) and no jitter, no
cap, and no overall deadline. That is fine on a laptop and wrong under load.
close_reason: All six children landed: jitter, :retry_max_delay, :deadline, :retry_on_status with retry-after, per-operation retry eligibility, and the latency table.

title: Per-call option values are not validated, only their names
description: 0.3.0 made an unknown per-call option raise. Its *value* is still sent unchecked. TypeDB.Config rejects answer_count_limit: 0 with 'invalid :answer_count_limit 0, expected a positive integer, or unset'; the same option on TypeDB.query/4 is forwarded, and 0 comes back as an empty answer with a server warning while -1, "10" and 1.5 come back as 400 HSR2 — the request-parse code, the same one an oversized body gets, saying nothing about which option was wrong. transaction_timeout_millis behaves the same, and 0 opens a transaction. TypeDB.Options.Query's own typespec says pos_integer() | nil, so these values contradict the driver's declared types and are passed through anyway.
design: Reuse Config's rules and its message text rather than writing a second set: the same option validated two ways is worse than validated once. ArgumentError, like a bad option name and a bad :transaction_type — an option value comes from the caller's own source.
acceptance_criteria: A per-call option value that Config would reject raises the same complaint, every constrained option is covered, and a test drives both levels against the same values so they cannot drift.
close_reason: TypeDB.CallOptions now checks option values as well as names, with the same rules TypeDB.Config applies (positive integers, timeouts, booleans), raising ArgumentError that names the option, the value and the call. nil stays 'unset' everywhere. A cross-level test drives both Config and every per-call function through the same table of bad values so the two cannot drift; it caught the first draft rejecting nil, which Config accepts.

title: TypeDB.stop/1 can crash the connection during shutdown
description: TypeDB.HTTP.Finch.terminate/1 calls Supervisor.stop(pid, :normal, 5_000) and catches only :exit. On OTP 29, proc_lib:stop/3 computes the remaining timeout after sys:terminate returns — 'T1 - ((monotonic_time(microsecond) + 999) div 1000 - T0)' — and if that reaches zero or below it ends up in 'receive ... after NegativeTimeout', which raises ErlangError :timeout_value rather than exiting. An error is not an exit, so the catch does not cover it and the crash propagates out of Connection.terminate/2. Observed twice while stopping many connections at once against unresponsive raw sockets: '** (ErlangError) Erlang error: :timeout_value ... lib/typedb/http/finch.ex:145: TypeDB.HTTP.Finch.terminate/1 ... lib/typedb/connection.ex:354'. The consequence is a crash report and a failed shutdown on a path whose whole job is to be best-effort.
acceptance_criteria: Stopping a connection cannot raise, whatever the pool does; a test covers a terminate that raises rather than exits.
close_reason: TypeDB.HTTP.Finch.terminate/1 catches errors as well as exits (OTP 29's proc_lib:stop/3 raises :timeout_value rather than exiting when the remaining timeout lands at or below zero), and Connection.terminate/2 contains anything an adapter's terminate/1 does. Covered by a test adapter that raises, throws, exits and errors; verified by removing the containment and watching three of five fail.

title: The README says TypeDB applies no answer cap. It caps at 10,000
description: README: 'The HTTP API is not streaming and TypeDB applies no cap of its own, so an unbounded match against a large database really does materialise the whole match set on the server and ship it.' Measured against 3.12.1: a match over 20,000 entities returns exactly 10,000 rows and sets warning "Read query results limit (10000) exceeded. Not all answers are returned." A server-side reduce count over the same data says 20,000, and passing answer_count_limit: 50_000 returns all 20,000 — so the option raises the cap as well as lowering it, which nothing says either. There is no server flag for it; the request option is the only control. A caller who reads the README, runs an unbounded match and counts what comes back silently loses every row past the ten-thousandth.
acceptance_criteria: The README and TypeDB.Options state the default cap and that the option raises it; the driver surfaces a server warning rather than leaving it to be read off the struct; an integration test pins the 10,000 default and the raised-limit behaviour.
close_reason: README/Config/Options corrected: TypeDB caps a read at 10,000 answers and :answer_count_limit raises that ceiling as well as lowering it; the driver now logs any server warning through the :log_level funnel; an integration test inserts 12,000 entities and pins all three behaviours. bench/answer_size.exs gives 'answers arrive whole' a number (488 B/row wire, 897 B/row decoded). A README section states where credentials live, backed by a test that no telemetry event carries the token or the password.

title: retryable?/1 says false for the one error it was written for
description: Error.retryable?/1's own doc example is a transaction that failed and a caller deciding whether to replay it. The canonical reason to replay a TypeDB transaction is an isolation conflict — two concurrent :write transactions touching the same data, where the loser's commit fails — and TypeDB answers that with code STC2 and status 400, so retryable?/1 returns false. Verified against a live 3.12.1: two transactions updating the same attribute, and two deleting the same entity, both produce '[STC2] Commit ... failed with isolation conflict: Transaction uses a lock held by a concurrent commit.' A caller following the documented example gives up on precisely the failure that retrying fixes.
acceptance_criteria: retryable?/1 is true for an isolation conflict, the codes it treats that way are public and documented like retryable_statuses/0, and an integration test provokes a real conflict rather than asserting the code from the stub.
close_reason: retryable?/1 now honours Error.retryable_codes/0 (STC2, the isolation conflict), pinned by an integration test that provokes a real conflict; the README, both guides and the docstring say how to re-run the block. to_struct's example carries the select stage it needs, and the ArgumentError names select as the fix.

title: A misspelled per-call option is silently ignored
description: TypeDB.Config rejects an unknown option to start_link/1, with a comment saying why: 'a misspelled option used to be accepted in silence and the default applied, so timout: 5_000 produced a connection that looked configured and was not.' Per-call options get no such treatment. TypeDB.query/4 reads :transaction_type, :commit, :given_rows, :timeout and :deadline out of the keyword list and ignores everything else, so given: [...] instead of given_rows: [...] runs the query unparameterised, and commmit: false commits. Found by running the published 0.2.2 package from a project that is not this one — the typo produced a server-side REP1 about a variable being both an Attribute and a Value, which names nothing that would lead anyone to the real mistake. Per CONTRIBUTING's rule this is program text, not data, so it raises ArgumentError rather than returning an error.
design: Raise ArgumentError, not {:error, %TypeDB.Error{}}: an option name can only come from the caller's own source, and no amount of error handling fixes it. Under 0.x this is a minor bump — code passing a stray option starts failing, which is the point.
acceptance_criteria: Every public function taking opts rejects a key it does not accept, naming the accepted ones. Covered by a test per function, and the option lists are checked against the functions' docs.
close_reason: TypeDB.CallOptions validates the option keys of every public function that takes them (query/4, transaction/5, Transaction.open/4, query/3, analyze/3, commit/2, rollback/2, close/2), raising ArgumentError that names the bad key, the call, and the accepted set. test/typedb/call_options_test.exs checks both directions plus a mechanical guard that every public function with a keyword() argument has a row in the table; both guards verified by breaking them.

title: Write an honest Limitations section
description:
Things a user will otherwise discover the hard way: answers are decoded whole,
so there is no streaming or pagination and a large match is a large term; a
connection points at one server with no failover; mix typedb.check needs a
POSIX shell; one Finch pool per connection; retries are blocking and happen in
the caller process.

None of these are bugs. All of them are surprises.
close_reason: Six operational limitations in the README, with the moduledoc pointing at them.

title: Write the guides
close_reason: Four guides written, linked from the README and shipped in the package. Getting-started deliberately omitted: the README is it, and it is the docs main page.

title: Add a fault-injecting HTTP adapter for tests
description:
The transport containment (lib/typedb/transport.ex contain/3) promises that no
adapter fault escapes as a bare exception. That promise is currently tested
with a handful of hand-written adapters.

Build one adapter that can be told to truncate the body, return malformed JSON,
answer with the wrong content type, return a 5xx storm, stall past the timeout,
raise, exit and throw - then assert across the whole public API that every
single one comes back as a %TypeDB.Error{}.
acceptance_criteria: Every public function is exercised against every fault mode; no fault produces an exception other than %TypeDB.Error{}; no fault kills the connection process.
close_reason: 13 faults x 25 public calls; the value-shape half of the assertion found analyze/3 returning {:ok, :ok} against its spec.

title: Property-based round-trip tests for the wire boundary
description:
Duration, DateTimeTZ, Given.encode_rows/1 and Concept.cast/2 are the pure
functions where TypeDB wire format meets Elixir types, and they are where the
subtle bugs have actually been: silent loss of the raw duration string,
NaiveDateTime precision changing under a round trip, decimals rendered with a
TypeQL suffix.

Example-based tests find the cases you thought of. StreamData finds the
nanosecond that rounds, the offset at the boundary, the string with the quote.
close_reason: Twelve properties over Duration, DateTimeTZ, Given and Concept; each verified by mutating the code it covers.

title: Matrix the optional dependencies
description:
The one bug that reached hex was a %Finch.Response{} struct pattern that made
the package fail to compile for anyone without finch - invisible to a matrix
that varied only Elixir and OTP. The same shape of bug is waiting in the
decimal and jason paths.

Add jobs: no optional deps at all; decimal present; jason present and JSON
absent. Compile and run the suite in each.
acceptance_criteria: A build with zero optional dependencies compiles and passes; removing the guard from any optional-dependency code path fails that job.
close_reason: Consumer application under test/support/consumer, run by CI with no optional deps and with all four; found and fixed the decimal suffix inconsistency.

title: Nightly run against the latest TypeDB release
description:
A scheduled workflow against TypeDB latest so that a server release breaks our
build before it breaks somebody application. Failure notifies rather than
blocks.
close_reason: Superseded: 'latest' is now in the integration matrix on every push, which covers the intent without a separate schedule that only fails at night.

title: Run the integration suite against more than one TypeDB version
description:
README says TypeDB 3.x. CI proves 3.12.1. Pick the oldest 3.x release the
driver claims and add it to the matrix alongside the newest - or narrow the
claim in the README to what is actually tested. Both are honest; the current
state is not.
close_reason: Measured 3.5.0 against the suite: broadly broken. Claim narrowed to 3.12+, matrix gains latest, floor-finding filed as tdb-vtg.6.

title: Decide the shape of Transaction.analyze/3
description:
analyze/3 returns TypeDB raw map, unmodelled and unversioned. Either give it a
struct like every other answer, or state in the docs that it is passed through
verbatim and tracks the server rather than this driver SemVer. It should be one
of those on purpose, not by omission.
design:
Decision: analyze/3 keeps returning TypeDB's raw map, and the docs now say explicitly that it is the one return value SemVer does not cover.

A struct would be a promise the driver cannot keep. The endpoint does not appear in TypeDB's published HTTP API reference, so its shape is neither specified nor stable; every server change would either break the struct or be silently dropped by it. Passing the map through means a TypeDB upgrade can change the shape inside a patch release of this driver, which is the honest description of what analysis output is.

Callers are told to match defensively and to build nothing load-bearing on it.
close_reason: Stays raw; documented as explicitly outside SemVer, with the reason.

title: Add ConceptRow.to_struct/2
description:
lib/typedb/concept_row.ex:96 spends an entire paragraph warning that
Kernel.struct/2 on a string-keyed map silently returns a struct full of nils,
and then shows the four-line incantation that avoids it. That paragraph is a
feature request with extra steps. Ship the safe version.
close_reason: to_struct/2 added with doctests and tests; the to_map/1 footgun paragraph replaced by a pointer to it.

title: Make the raise-vs-return rule uniform across the public API
description:
TypeDB.query/4 raises ArgumentError for an unknown :transaction_type
(lib/typedb.ex:178). Transaction.open/4 raises FunctionClauseError for the same
mistake. Config.new/1 returns {:error, %TypeDB.Error{kind: :config}}. Three
answers to one question.

Pick the rule - programmer error raises, runtime input returns - write it in
CONTRIBUTING, then make the code and the api_convention test enforce it.
close_reason: Rule written in CONTRIBUTING; Transaction.open/4 raises ArgumentError by name; enforced by a test on the enum arguments and on the :encode raises.

title: Pin the real server error codes for every operation
description:
The unit suite asserts the codes the stub returns, and the audit already found
four places where the stub had invented codes the server does not use (M9,
M9b - a single made-up USR2 standing in for SRV4, USU4 and USD3). Four found by
looking at one endpoint is evidence about the endpoints nobody looked at.

Enumerate the failure of every operation against a live server, record the code
and status, and assert them in the integration suite so the stub can be checked
against reality instead of trusted.
close_reason: Every failing operation probed against a live 3.12.1; five stub codes corrected; integration test pins them all.

title: Add TypeDB.Error.retryable?/1
description:
Callers who want their own retry loop currently have to write
kind in [:transport, :timeout], which is driver internals copied into user
code - and it goes stale the moment A4 makes some :server errors retryable.
One predicate, owned by the driver, tested against every kind.
close_reason: retryable?/1 and retryable_statuses/0 added; the default list is defined once and the agreement is tested.

title: Add a :log_level connection option
description:
Five Logger call sites, three levels, four modules, and no way for an
application to quieten the driver short of filtering the global Logger by
module. A library that cannot be turned down gets turned off.

Add :log_level (default matching current behaviour, :none accepted) and one
table in the docs listing every line the driver can emit, at what level, with
what metadata.
close_reason: :log_level added as a per-connection floor; all logging behind TypeDB.Log; docs list every line; metadata keys now guarded by a test rather than by credo.

title: Raise the level of the failures that currently whisper
description:
Retry exhaustion logs nothing. A failed token renewal logs nothing. Both are
production incidents in miniature and both should be :warning. The retry
attempts themselves stay at :debug - they are noise until they are not.
close_reason: Warning on exhaustion and on failed renewal; [:typedb, :retry, :exhausted] event with :attempts.

title: Emit an event when retries are exhausted
description:
Giving up after :max_retries is currently invisible: the caller gets an
ordinary error, indistinguishable from a first-attempt failure, and the only
trace that the driver tried five times is a Logger.debug that nobody has
enabled. Retry exhaustion is a signal that something upstream is broken and it
should be countable.
close_reason: Warning on exhaustion and on failed renewal; [:typedb, :retry, :exhausted] event with :attempts.

title: Ship TypeDB.Telemetry.attach_default_logger/1
description:
Finch, Ecto, Oban and Broadway all ship one, because the gap between "the
driver emits telemetry" and "I can see what my app is doing" is otherwise an
afternoon of handler plumbing per project. One function, a documented log
level, off by default.
close_reason: attach_default_logger/1 and detach_default_logger/0 added, documented and tested in a non-async module.

title: Narrow retry eligibility from HTTP method to operation
description:
lib/typedb/transport.ex:122 decides idempotence by method: GET and DELETE
retry, everything else does not. That is safe but blunt. POST
/v1/transactions/open is perfectly safe to retry, and so is a read-only
/v1/query - both are currently one-shot, so a single dropped packet fails a
query the driver could have transparently recovered.

Meanwhile commit must never be retried and correctly is not. Move the decision
to the call sites that know the semantics, keeping the method rule as the
default for anything that does not say.
close_reason: Every call site now sets :idempotent from what the operation does; method rule kept as the default.

title: Retry retryable HTTP statuses and honour Retry-After
description:
lib/typedb/transport.ex:127 retries only kind :transport and :timeout. A
TypeDB behind a proxy, an ingress or a load balancer answers 502/503/504 while
it restarts, and 429 when it is shedding load. None of those is retried, so the
driver gives up instantly on exactly the failures that retrying was built for.

Add a configurable retryable-status set (429, 502, 503, 504 by default) and
honour a Retry-After header when present, clamped by :retry_max_delay.
close_reason: :retry_on_status defaulting to [429,502,503,504], retry-after honoured and capped by :retry_max_delay, idempotence gate unchanged.

title: Documentation a stranger can start from
description:
Reference docs are complete (every public function has a moduledoc and specs).
What is missing is the narrative layer and an honest statement of limits.
close_reason: Four guides, a Livebook notebook, an honest Limitations section, and docs groups ordered as a table of contents and held there by a test.

title: Test depth: properties, fault injection, soak
description:
349 unit tests across three adapters is good coverage of the paths we thought
of. The bugs that got through were in the paths we did not: precision loss on a
round trip, an optional dependency being absent, a stub disagreeing with the
server. Those three classes each have a mechanical answer.
close_reason: Property tests, a 13-fault x 25-call matrix that found a real analyze/3 bug, a bounded soak, and an enforced coverage floor.

title: Compatibility matrix and CI hardening
description:
README claims TypeDB 3.x; CI proves 3.12.1. Either widen the proof or narrow
the claim. Also: the one bug that reached hex (a %Finch.Response{} struct
pattern in an optional-dependency code path) was invisible to a CI matrix that
only varied Elixir and OTP.
close_reason: All six children closed: multi-version integration matrix, nightly latest run, optional-dependency matrix, PLT caching, Windows job, and a measured TypeDB floor of 3.12.0.

title: Error taxonomy, containment and predicates
description:
Every failure is supposed to be a %TypeDB.Error{} with a stable :kind and
TypeDB code. Two things are unfinished: public functions that still raise
ArgumentError/FunctionClauseError for bad input, and the absence of any
predicate telling a caller whether an error is worth retrying.
close_reason: retryable?/1, uniform raise-or-return rule, real error codes pinned, message/1 carries the status.

title: Nothing says a request body cannot exceed 2 MiB
description: TypeDB's HTTP API refuses a request body over 2 MiB and there is no server flag for it. Bisected against 3.12.1: 2047 KiB is accepted, 2048 KiB is not. The failure has two shapes — just over the line gives 400 HSR2 ('Failed to buffer the request body: length limit exceeded'), while far over (15 MiB, 31 MiB) closes the socket, which the driver reports as :transport and Error.retryable?/1 calls retryable, so max_retries re-sends a body that can never succeed. The recipes guide tells people to bulk load in batches of 2,000 rows without saying that the ceiling is bytes rather than rows: 2,000 rows of 200-byte notes is 620 KiB and fine, the same 2,000 rows with 1 KiB notes is not.
acceptance_criteria: The bulk-load recipe batches by payload size and names the 2 MiB ceiling, TypeDB.Transaction.query/3 says it, the errors guide lists HSR2, and an integration test pins the boundary so a server-side change to it fails a build.
close_reason: 2 MiB request-body limit bisected against 3.12.1 (2047 KiB accepted, 2048 KiB not), documented in the recipes guide with a byte-aware chunk_while that was itself run against a live server, in the errors guide's code table, and on Transaction.query/3. An integration test pins both sides of the boundary. Also recorded that a body far over the limit closes the socket and therefore presents as a retryable :transport failure.

title: A recipes guide: the patterns, not the mechanics
description: The four guides explain how the driver works — transactions, errors, telemetry, testing — and none of them shows how to do the things an application actually needs. Paging a match around TypeDB's 10,000-answer cap, bulk loading, upsert, counting without fetching, mapping rows onto structs, migrating a schema at boot. I wrote each of those by hand while dogfooding and had to work them out from scratch every time, which is the definition of a documentation gap.
acceptance_criteria: Every recipe has been run against a live TypeDB 3.12.1 and its output is what the guide says it is; the guide is published with the docs and its code blocks are parsed by the suite.
close_reason: guides/recipes.md covers paging (and why sort is not optional), streaming, bulk load, upsert and why put is not one, counting, batch delete, to_struct, and a boot-time migration. Every recipe was run against a live 3.12.1 before it was written down, and test/integration/recipes_integration_test.exs runs the same queries on every push.

title: CI never runs the token-renewal or TLS suites
description: Two opt-in suites verify headline claims — 'tokens handled for you' and secure TLS defaults — and neither has ever run in CI, because each needs a server started with flags a GitHub Actions service container cannot override. They are therefore verified only when someone remembers to do it by hand, which is the pattern this project has spent four releases eliminating. Both were run by hand today against 3.12.1 and pass: token renewal against a second server with --server.authentication.token-expiration-seconds 5, and the TLS suite (including the hostname-mismatch case, via an /etc/hosts entry) through all three adapters against a server started with --server.encryption.enabled.
design: A service container cannot have its command overridden, so start these with 'docker run -d' in an ordinary step instead. The TLS job mints its own CA and server certificate with openssl and mounts them in.
acceptance_criteria: Both suites run on every push, and a failure in either fails the build.
close_reason: ci.yml gained token_renewal and tls jobs, both starting TypeDB with docker run because a service container cannot take the flags they need. Verified green in CI (run 30745938744) with the token suite taking 27s and the TLS suite reporting '3 passed' per adapter — not skips. Each job now fails if its suite skips itself.

title: Nothing tests that the :schema default serialises
description: README and the TypeDB moduledoc both warn that :transaction_type defaults to :schema, that a :schema transaction takes an exclusive database-wide lock, and that one-shot queries left on the default therefore serialise. It is the most likely performance mistake a new user makes and nothing in the suite checks it. Proved by hand against 3.12.1: holding a :schema transaction open for 1000ms makes a concurrent one-shot on the default take 1004ms, while a one-shot :read takes 1ms; a held :read blocks nothing.
acceptance_criteria: An integration test holds a :schema transaction and shows that a default one-shot waits for it while a :read one-shot does not.
close_reason: Integration test holds a :schema transaction for 500ms and asserts a one-shot on the default waits for it while a one-shot :read does not; verified non-vacuous by switching the blocked call to :read and watching it fail. README now states the measured behaviour rather than only naming the lock.

title: The testing guide's retry example does not retry
description: guides/testing.md offers a FlakyAdapter that fails the first two requests and says 'two failures then a success exercises the retry path end to end'. Run it as written and the call fails: :max_retries defaults to 1, so two failures exhaust the budget and the example demonstrates the give-up path instead. Verified in a consumer project against a live server — with max_retries: 2 it succeeds on the third attempt and logs both retries. The guide's code is otherwise correct, which is what makes the claim worth fixing rather than deleting.
acceptance_criteria: The example produces the behaviour the surrounding text claims, and a test drives the guide's own adapter code so the claim cannot rot back.
close_reason: guides/testing.md now sets max_retries: 2 so its two injected failures actually exercise the retry path; test/typedb/guide_test.exs compiles the guide's own FlakyAdapter and drives both outcomes, asserts the guide still carries the option, and parses every elixir block in every guide and the README.

title: to_struct's documented example raises
description: The example on ConceptRow.to_struct is 'match $p isa person, has name $name, has age $age;' piped into to_struct(Person), showing [%Person{name: "Alice", age: 31}]. Run it: $p is bound too, Person has no :p field, and to_struct raises ArgumentError. Every ordinary match binds the entity variable, so the function is unusable without a select stage — which is the right answer, and is exactly what the docs do not say. Found by using the published package from another project.
acceptance_criteria: The documented example runs as documented (it is a doctest, or it carries the select stage), and the ArgumentError names TypeQL's select as the fix.
close_reason: retryable?/1 now honours Error.retryable_codes/0 (STC2, the isolation conflict), pinned by an integration test that provokes a real conflict; the README, both guides and the docstring say how to re-run the block. to_struct's example carries the select stage it needs, and the ArgumentError names select as the fix.

title: A whole row cannot be read as native Elixir terms
description: ConceptRow.typed_value/2 returns a Decimal, a Duration or a DateTime; to_map/1 and to_struct/2 return the wire value, so the same row reads as %TypeDB.Duration{} one variable at a time and "P1Y2M3DT4H5M6S" all at once. Found by using the published package from another project: the README's headline promises 'TypeDB's temporal and decimal types available as native Elixir terms', and the two functions that convert a whole row are the ones that do not. Adding to_typed_map/1 and a :typed option to to_struct/2 is additive; changing what to_map/1 returns is not, and is not proposed.
acceptance_criteria: A row of every TypeDB value type reads natively in one call, the asymmetry with to_map/1 is documented on both functions, and the API snapshot records the addition.
close_reason: Added ConceptRow.to_typed_map/1 and typed: true on to_struct/3; to_map/1 is unchanged and now documents that it is the wire form on purpose. Covered by unit tests and by an integration test that reads a row of every TypeDB value type back from a live server — which caught that TypeDB pads datetime to microseconds.

title: Establish the oldest TypeDB the driver actually supports
description:
The README now says 3.12 or newer, which is what has been measured rather than
what is true. 3.12.1 passes the whole suite; 3.5.0 fails broadly — `given` rows
are rejected with HSR2, `/v1/servers` answers 404, several error codes differ,
and insert-then-match fails. Everything between is unknown.

Bisecting by hand is slow because each step is a download, a server start and a
full suite run. CI can do it in parallel for free: a workflow_dispatch job with
a matrix over 3.7.3, 3.8.3, 3.10.4, 3.11.5 and continue-on-error, run once,
answers it in one go. Then narrow or widen the README to the true floor and put
that version in the permanent matrix as the lower bound.
close_reason: Floor is 3.12.0, measured: 3.12.0 passes the integration suite whole, 3.11.5 fails 14 tests (no given stage; User.delete answers 400 not 404), 3.5.0 fails more broadly. No published 3.6.x/3.9.x, so 3.11.5 and 3.12.0 are adjacent. 3.12.0 added to the CI matrix; .github/workflows/compat.yml re-runs the bisect on demand.

title: Commit the benchmarks the CHANGELOG quotes
description:
The CHANGELOG publishes ~1900 req/s for Finch against 77 for httpc at 200-way
concurrency. Those scripts live in a scratch directory that no longer exists.
Numbers in a changelog that nobody can reproduce are decoration; put them under
bench/ and re-run them for the 1.0 notes.
close_reason: Decimal resolution memoised in :persistent_term (1099ms -> 5ms per 50k casts without the dependency); bench/decode.exs and bench/transport.exs committed and re-run, CHANGELOG corrected from their output.

title: Resolve Decimal once, not per value
description:
lib/typedb/concept.ex:240 calls Code.ensure_loaded?(Decimal) for every decimal
attribute cast. It is cheap and it is cached, and it is still a lookup on the
hot path of a query that returns ten thousand rows. Resolve it at compile time
or once per connection.
close_reason: Decimal resolution memoised in :persistent_term (1099ms -> 5ms per 50k casts without the dependency); bench/decode.exs and bench/transport.exs committed and re-run, CHANGELOG corrected from their output.

title: Decide whether 1.0 supports multiple servers
description:
TypeDB.Server.servers/1 returns cluster membership. Nothing consumes it. A
connection has one :url.

For TypeDB CE that is correct and complete. For anyone running more than one
node it means the driver has no answer for a node going away, and they will
find that out during an incident.

The decision is in or out. If out, say so in the Limitations section (G2) and
close this. If in, H2 follows.
design:
Decision: out of 1.0. A connection keeps one :url.

Failover is only worth shipping if it is tested against a real multi-node cluster, and this project's whole discipline has been to check claims against a live server — that is why the supported TypeDB range is what was measured rather than what ought to work, and why five invented error codes were replaced with recorded ones. TypeDB CE is single-node, so there is nothing available to test failover against. Shipping it would be a promise backed by nothing, which is the failure mode the rest of the roadmap has been removing.

A load balancer in front of a cluster solves the same problem outside the driver, and the Limitations section says so.

Accepting :urls later is purely additive: it needs no slot held open in 1.0, so deciding 'out' costs nothing but a minor version when someone with a cluster wants it. tdb-1j9.2 is closed on that basis rather than deleted.
close_reason: Out of 1.0: failover untestable without a multi-node cluster, and every other claim in this driver is measured. Recorded in the issue design notes and in the README's Limitations.

title: Review the ex_doc module groups
description:
Once the internals are hidden, the remaining grouping should be re-read as a
table of contents rather than a list of files.
close_reason: Groups reordered into reading order, Answers split out, mix task grouped; a test asserts the grouping covers the published surface exactly.

title: Publish a Livebook
description:
Mix.install, a local TypeDB in Docker, schema, insert, match, transactions. It
is the fastest way for someone to find out whether this driver fits, and it is
worth a Run in Livebook badge on the README.
close_reason: notebooks/getting_started.livemd, badged and rendered in the docs, with tests that parse its blocks and check the version it installs.

title: Set a coverage floor
description:
Coverage is measured and never enforced. Set the floor at the current number
so it can only go up.
close_reason: Bounded soak in the integration suite (runs on every push); coverage floor at 85% enforced by a CI step, verified by raising it.

title: Put a bounded concurrency soak in CI
description:
The 200-way burst and the token-expiry-straddling transactions were run by
hand during the audit and their results are quoted in the CHANGELOG. A bounded
version belongs in the integration job so the claim keeps being true.
close_reason: Bounded soak in the integration suite (runs on every push); coverage floor at 85% enforced by a CI step, verified by raising it.

title: Compile and unit-test on Windows
description:
mix typedb.check needs a POSIX shell by decision, and that is written down.
The driver itself is pure Elixir and should be proven to work on Windows rather
than assumed to.
close_reason: windows-latest job compiles and runs the unit suite through all three adapters.

title: Cache the dialyzer PLT
description: Minutes per run, every run, for a cache key that is just the lock file.
close_reason: Already in ci.yml: actions/cache on _build/dev/*.plt keyed by mix.lock, on the lint job. Verified in the run for db4314e, where the step reports success.

title: Write the versioning policy
description:
What 1.0 covers: public function signatures, error kinds and codes, telemetry
event names and metadata keys, the config option set, the transport behaviour.
What it does not: internal modules, the exact text of messages, TypeDB own wire
format. Without this written down, every bug fix is arguably a breaking change.
close_reason: Covered/not-covered lists added to CONTRIBUTING's Versioning section.

title: Make Exception.message/1 consistently useful
description:
A %TypeDB.Error{} carries kind, code, status, message and reason but the
rendered message does not always include the request that produced it. When
this lands in a log line or an exit reason it should say what was attempted.
close_reason: message/1 renders kind, status and code; tested for every combination of present and absent.

title: Put :database and :transaction_id in request metadata
description:
lib/typedb/transport.ex:163 builds metadata of connection, method, path and
attempt. Grouping metrics by database - the first thing anyone does on a
multi-tenant server - means regex-parsing :path. Both values are known at the
call site.
close_reason: :database, :transaction_type and :transaction_id on operation and request spans; :metadata request option added for what the path cannot carry.

title: Document the latency arithmetic
description:
Once A1-A4 land, the TypeDB moduledoc should state, in one short table, what a
call can cost in the worst case for the default configuration. Right now a
reader has to derive it from three separate options.
close_reason: Table plus worst-case expression in the TypeDB moduledoc.

title: Cluster and availability: decide in or out for 1.0
description:
TypeDB.Server.servers/1 returns the cluster membership and nothing in the
driver uses it. A single connection points at a single URL. This is either a
1.0 feature or a documented non-feature; drifting is the only bad answer.
close_reason: Decided: out of 1.0, with the reason recorded and the limitation stated in the README.

title: Performance: keep the numbers honest and the hot path clean
description:
The CHANGELOG publishes throughput numbers that live only in a scratch
directory, and the value-casting path calls Code.ensure_loaded?/1 per value.
close_reason: Decimal resolution memoised in :persistent_term (1099ms -> 5ms per 50k casts without the dependency); bench/decode.exs and bench/transport.exs committed and re-run, CHANGELOG corrected from their output.

title: The 'given is the fast way to write many rows' claim has no number
description: Both README and Transaction.query/3 say a given stage is the fast way to write many rows — one request and one query compilation instead of N — without measuring it. The honest competitor is not N requests but one request whose query text carries N insert statements, since that is also a single round trip.
acceptance_criteria: bench/given.exs measures all three and the figures are published where the claim is made.
close_reason: bench/given.exs measures all three strategies; at 2,000 rows given_rows is 101ms against 1541ms for one request carrying 2,000 insert statements and 8830ms for 2,000 requests. Published in the README and on Transaction.query/3.

title: 'Answers arrive whole' has no number
description: The README's first limitation is that the HTTP API is not streaming, so an answer is materialised entirely in memory. It does not say what that costs, which is the only thing a reader needs in order to decide whether it matters to them. :answer_count_limit is offered as the protection without a figure for what it is protecting against. Measure the decoded size of a large answer and publish it.
acceptance_criteria: The Limitations section carries a measured bytes-per-row figure and the arithmetic for a large match, produced by a script under bench/.
close_reason: README/Config/Options corrected: TypeDB caps a read at 10,000 answers and :answer_count_limit raises that ceiling as well as lowering it; the driver now logs any server warning through the :log_level funnel; an integration test inserts 12,000 entities and pins all three behaviours. bench/answer_size.exs gives 'answers arrive whole' a number (488 B/row wire, 897 B/row decoded). A README section states where credentials live, backed by a test that no telemetry event carries the token or the password.

title: Document where credentials actually live
description: The security tests pin that the password and a static token never reach the ETS table, an inspect, or a crash report — verified again by hand against a live server. Nothing user-facing says so, and nothing says the opposite half: the issued bearer token IS in the connection's :protected ETS table, readable by any process in the node, necessarily, because requests run in the caller's process. Someone auditing the driver has to read connection.ex to learn either fact.
acceptance_criteria: The README states what is held where, what is redacted, and which of those is a design consequence rather than an oversight.
close_reason: README/Config/Options corrected: TypeDB caps a read at 10,000 answers and :answer_count_limit raises that ceiling as well as lowering it; the driver now logs any server warning through the :log_level funnel; an integration test inserts 12,000 entities and pins all three behaviours. bench/answer_size.exs gives 'answers arrive whole' a number (488 B/row wire, 897 B/row decoded). A README section states where credentials live, backed by a test that no telemetry event carries the token or the password.

title: Duration.parse/1 is 40x slower than every other cast
description: bench/decode.exs measures cast duration at 16.0us/value against 0.37us for decimal, 0.43us for datetime-tz and 0.10us for string. An answer of 10,000 durations spends 160ms in the parser. Nothing depends on this yet — durations are rare in real schemas — but the number is now published in a benchmark, so it is a question a reader can ask. Find out where it goes: the regex, the segment-by-segment Integer.parse, or building the %TypeDB.Duration{}.
acceptance_criteria: Either the per-value cost is brought into line with the other casts, or bench/README.md records why it cannot be and the issue is closed as won't-fix.
close_reason: Duration.parse/1 was running a regex per component with a trailing (.*) that copied the remainder each time: 16us/value. Replaced with a length scan plus a slice, keeping Integer.parse/Float.parse for the arithmetic so no float rounds differently. 1.63us/value, verified identical over 200,000 generated well-formed and malformed durations against the previous implementation.

title: Write a release checklist
description:
Tag, CI gate, hex publish, docs, CHANGELOG, GitHub release. It ran off memory
and a rewritten workflow file for 0.1.0. Write it down before the second
release proves memory does not scale.
close_reason: CONTRIBUTING's Releasing section is now a checklist: decide the number from the api-snapshot diff, prepare (beads, version, CHANGELOG heading and link, README and notebook pins, the release paragraph), run the full gate including the integration and TypeQL jobs the release workflow deliberately skips, read mix hex.build's file list, tag, then what to do when the run fails before or after mix hex.publish.

title: Set the repository topics and homepage
description:
Needs a human with repo admin - no MCP tool in the agent session exposes
repository settings.

  gh repo edit NoeticEcho/TypedbEx --homepage "https://hexdocs.pm/typedb" \
    --add-topic elixir --add-topic typedb --add-topic database \
    --add-topic driver --add-topic graph-database --add-topic typeql

Purely findability.
close_reason: Topics (database, driver, elixir, graph-database, typedb, typeql) and homepage (https://hexdocs.pm/typedb) are set on the repository; verified through the GitHub API.

title: Document the beads workflow in CONTRIBUTING
description:
A contributor cloning the repo finds a .beads directory and no explanation.
Cover: install bd, bd init --from-jsonl to seed from the committed export until
the Dolt remote exists, bd ready to find work, bd update --claim, and the
convention of naming the issue id in the commit message so bd doctor can spot
orphans.
close_reason: Documented in CONTRIBUTING.md: install, bd ready, claim/close, seeding a fresh clone, and that issues.jsonl is an export rather than the source of truth.

title: Implement multi-address connections with failover
description:
Only if H1 says in. Accept :urls, health-check members, fail over on
:transport errors, refresh membership from /v1/servers. Substantial: it touches
config validation, the connection state machine and every retry decision, and
it needs a multi-node integration environment to test honestly.
close_reason: Not for 1.0, per tdb-1j9.1. Accepting :urls is additive, so it can land in a minor release when someone with a cluster to test against wants it.

title: Release housekeeping
description: Small, mostly outside the code, mostly needing a human.
close_reason: Topics (database, driver, elixir, graph-database, typedb, typeql) and homepage (https://hexdocs.pm/typedb) are set on the repository; verified through the GitHub API.
